assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern monetary-policy framework transformed macroeconomic analysis and policy discussion by making nominal rigidities, expectations, and welfare-based policy analysis operational.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's tractable rigidity, Taylor's policy-rule analysis, and Woodford's general-equilibrium monetary theory provide a coherent core, though the broader programme has many major contributors.
assessment.maturity: Its theoretical and policy influence has endured for decades and has been tested through multiple monetary-policy episodes.
uncertainties: The proposed discovery encompasses a large intellectual programme, making a three-person allocation necessarily incomplete.
The appropriate balance between foundational theory and later New Keynesian synthesis remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral-based amplification and financial-accelerator mechanisms supplied a durable account of how financial conditions can magnify aggregate fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore established the central collateral-cycle mechanism, while Gertler was central to the financial-accelerator formulation and its macroeconomic application.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are longstanding, highly integrated into macroeconomic models, and especially salient after repeated credit disruptions.
uncertainties: Credit-cycle mechanisms have overlapping antecedents and later extensions.
The division of credit between the collateral-constraint and financial-accelerator strands is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods made forward-looking individual decisions empirically tractable and changed applied structural work across labour, industrial organization, and public economics.
assessment.attribution: Rust's foundational framework and Keane's major methodological and applied contributions form a clear core; credit to additional contributors is plausible but less indispensable to the central recognition.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been used and refined over several decades, with broad and continuing empirical influence.
uncertainties: Structural estimation remains sensitive to modelling assumptions and is not the sole empirical approach to dynamic behavior.
The proper laureate set could reasonably include other pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation programme provided a powerful quantitative framework for relating distorted factor allocation to productivity and international income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow supplied a landmark empirical-quantitative formulation, while Restuccia made central contributions to the broader theoretical and quantitative programme.
assessment.maturity: The framework is widely used, has stimulated extensive measurement work, and remains a central benchmark in development and growth.
uncertainties: Mapping observed dispersion into distortions is model-dependent.
The empirical size and policy interpretation of misallocation effects remain actively debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reshaped the theory and measurement of trade gains, explaining patterns inaccessible to representative-firm models.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the indispensable originator of the canonical model; Helpman and Redding made major related theoretical and empirical contributions to the wider programme.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been deeply absorbed into trade research and applied policy analysis over more than two decades.
uncertainties: The contribution may be most cleanly attributable to a narrower set than the listed programme.
Quantitative welfare conclusions depend materially on model structure and elasticities.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Modern political economics gave systematic theoretical and empirical accounts of how political institutions, state capacity, and fiscal choices jointly shape economic development.
assessment.attribution: Besley, Persson, and Tabellini are leading architects of complementary strands linking political incentives and institutions to policy outcomes.
assessment.maturity: The programme is well established and influential across political economy, public finance, and development.
uncertainties: Its intellectual boundaries overlap with earlier institutional and political-economy traditions.
Causal identification of institutional mechanisms remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work fundamentally improved understanding of how technology and trade shocks affect local labour markets, occupational tasks, and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor's task framework and the Autor-Dorn-Hanson evidence on local adjustment provide a particularly recognizable core of the discovery.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a large literature and materially influenced both research and public debate.
uncertainties: Separating technology, trade, and broader local adjustment mechanisms is empirically challenging.
The candidate description combines several related but distinct research programmes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models made the distributional and marginal-propensity-to-consume channels of macroeconomic policy quantitatively central.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante provided a defining formulation and a clear common contribution to the modern HANK literature.
assessment.maturity: The framework has rapidly become influential in contemporary macroeconomics and policy analysis.
uncertainties: The literature is comparatively recent and still evolving.
Its empirical quantitative implications and the appropriate allocation of credit across related heterogeneous-agent work require further settling.
